title: Sistema Katu Balam, Akumal - Laden, Luke, Pugliese 2011
credits: Sistema Katu Balam, Quintana Roo; topografiado con Suuntos y medidor láser 28-30 de marzo 2011 por Juan Laden, Barbara Luke y Mike Pugliese; longitud 861 m, profundidad 10 m; dibujado por Barbara Luke (Canadian Caver 75, p. 8, 2012)
sistemaWhy: Not in the database: no sistema or cave name or aka contains Katu (the import's 'Uxuxubi' match is only its aka 'Balam', another cave). Mapbox/OSM have no Katu Balam either.
unverified: No position at all: Sistema Katu Balam (West, East and Lord of the Ticks entrances) is in neither the database (names and akas), OpenStreetMap (Overpass name search over Quintana Roo) nor a web search (only the mexicancaves.org listing 'Katu Balam, Sist., Akumal'), and the map draws no road, coast, other cenote or coordinate. The single control point is a NOMINAL anchor (the East Entrance put on OpenStreetMap's Akumal village node, from the map's 'Akumal' filing), so the pipeline can run: the geometry is NOT on the ground. It shares that anchor with maps/knock-out.json (also nominal), so the two overlap. To fix: field GPS of two of the three entrances (West to Lord of the Ticks is about 128 m).
placementWhy: UNVERIFIED (see 'unverified'). Scale from the 0-50 m bar: 0 at x 544.5, 50 at x 1422 (y 1436), 877.5 px = 50 m, 0.0570 m/px; its five 10 m ticks are evenly spaced (175.5 px). The section below, at the same scale, spans the plan's A-A' length. North: the 'Ng' arrow (norte geográfico) points straight up: angle 0. Position nominal.

trace.minHoleSqMetresWhy: the pillars are small (0.3 to 12 m2); the default 60 m2 dropped them all
trace.wallSimplifyMetresWhy: a small map (0.057 m/px): the default 0.5 m cuts the scalloped walls into straight segments
trace.minLineMetresWhy: the small pillars' rings are 1-3 m long; the default 1 m dropped most
trace.minOutlineMetresWhy: PROPOSED KEY (trace_scan.py hard-codes MIN_OUTLINE_METRES = 8 m): the pillars' rings are 1.5-8 m long. Until the script reads it, trace with the prototype wrapper scratchpad kb/trace_kb.py
trace.labelBoxesWhy: 'West Entrance' and the west 'sump', which OCR misses (printed over the grey screen / beside the dashed end)

prep.why: b/w drawing: thin wall outline, flooded parts in a halftone grey screen, dry floor white with stipple, pillars as bold closed outlines. fill_passages.py tints the area enclosed by the outer wall.

sealLines.why: open end of the Sink or Swim Passage (the 'low airspace dig', walls end with ticks)
the east wall where the 'calcite raft dunes' label touches it (the label's mask cut it)

prep.islandPointsWhy: the rock pillars: closed outlines drawn with the walls' scalloped bold stroke, white inside (found by a prototype, scratchpad kb/isl.py: enclosed white areas of 90 px or more, at least 3.5 px deep, whose edge is mostly ink); fill_passages' own bold test needs strokes of 5 px or more and finds none here (strokes about 3-4 px). A few small pillars whose outline isn't closed on the scan stay as details.
prep.closePxWhy: 5 leaves gaps in the thin outer wall (the cave is not enclosed); 7 closes it with no bridge across the exterior
prep.labelBoxesWhy: 'calcite raft' touches the east wall and isn't among the OCR labels fill_passages masks: its letters were tinted as passage

symbols.why: Barbara Luke's UIS-style drawing (Canadian Caver 2012): no legend, no letter codes, no depths in the plan (only the title's 'Profundidad: 10 m'), no water-flow arrows (the small wavy ticks scattered over the floor have no arrowheads and no legend: floor ripples or slopes, not flow), no bones (none drawn or written; every part of the plan checked by eye at full size), no 'To ...' pointers. Kept by hand: the three sumps, the named rooms and passages, and the feature notes (thick root masses, calcite rafts, smelly organics, calcite raft dunes) as place names at what they label; 'small swimming lead' as unexplored; 'low airspace dig' (the Sink or Swim Passage's dug end) as a place name.
